title: argparse positional slot swallows '--flag-with-trailing-space'
description: argparse accepts '--definitely-not-a-real-flag- ' (with trailing whitespace) as a positional argument instead of rejecting it with rc=2 because the parser has a positional `value` slot and the token has no '=' separator. __main__.py:86 then hands the bad token to parse(), which raises OrdinalDateParseError; __main__:91 re-raises (default parse path), Python prints a traceback, exit rc=1. The harness asserts rc==2 for mode==5 (harness_cli.py:135) and crashes. Library itself behaves correctly (parse() rejects the bad input with the documented exception class); the issue is UX polish on the CLI entry point and the harness's over-strict mode==5 assertion.
recommendations: Wrap parse() in __main__.py:86 with try/except OrdinalDateParseError on the default (parse) path; print clean message + return 2.
OR: subclass argparse.ArgumentParser to reject '--' tokens that don't match a defined option BEFORE the positional slot accepts them.
OR (lowest risk): relax harness_cli.py:135 from `assert rc == 2` to `assert rc in (1, 2)` to allow the CLI fuzzer to run to completion. This is harness-only; library and repo behaviour unchanged.
